Taper and stem profiles

Source: vignettes/taper-profiles.Rmd
taper-profiles.Rmd

Stem functions return diameters, heights, and cumulative volumes for checking the modeled stem. Inputs use inches and feet, and volumes use cubic feet.

## Select a tree for the profile
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree_id == 5)

## Measure the stem profile
profile <- stem_profile(
  tree_id = tree$tree_id,
  dbh = tree$dbh,
  ht = tree$ht,
  spcd = tree$spcd,
  model = tree$model,
  step = 1
)

step is spacing in feet along the stem. Cumulative volume starts at the lower bound.

The solid and dashed lines show inside and outside bark diameters.

Diameters and heights 

## Calculate dib
dib(dbh = tree$dbh,
    ht = tree$ht,
    h = 20,
    spcd = tree$spcd,
    model = tree$model) %>%
  rename(`diameter inside bark (inches)` = value)
#>   diameter inside bark (inches) status
#> 1                      15.63832      0

## Calculate dob
dob(dbh = tree$dbh,
    ht = tree$ht,
    h = 20,
    spcd = tree$spcd,
    model = tree$model) %>%
  rename(`diameter outside bark (inches)` = value)
#>   diameter outside bark (inches) status
#> 1                        16.7571      0

## Calculate height at dib
height_at_dib(dbh = tree$dbh,
              ht = tree$ht,
              dib = 6,
              spcd = tree$spcd,
              model = tree$model) %>%
  rename(`height (feet)` = value)
#>   height (feet) status
#> 1       76.7227      0

## Calculate height at dob
height_at_dob(dbh = tree$dbh,
              ht = tree$ht,
              dob = 6,
              spcd = tree$spcd,
              model = tree$model) %>%
  rename(`height (feet)` = value)
#>   height (feet) status
#> 1      78.34176      0

Diameter results use inches. Inverse results use feet and retain the highest crossing when several exist. Status identifies unavailable measurements and multiple crossings.

Taper registry

has_inverse records a model-provided inverse. Numeric inversion remains available for the selected model when this flag is false.

## List models for the selected species
models <- taper_models(spcd = tree$spcd)
id form has_dob has_inverse has_integral
100FW2W202 flewelling_2pt TRUE FALSE TRUE
100JB2W202 r1_taper FALSE TRUE TRUE
200CZ2W202 r2_taper FALSE TRUE TRUE
200CZ3W202 r2_taper FALSE TRUE TRUE
200FW2W202 flewelling_2pt TRUE FALSE TRUE
300FW2W202 flewelling_2pt TRUE FALSE TRUE 
## Inspect the selected model
get_taper_model(model = tree$model)$id
#> [1] "F00FW2W202"

## Check model capabilities
taper_models() %>%
  filter(id == tree$model) %>%
  select(id, has_dob, has_inverse, has_integral)
#>           id has_dob has_inverse has_integral
#> 1 F00FW2W202    TRUE       FALSE         TRUE

## Check availability and species scope
has_taper_model(model = tree$model)
#> [1] TRUE

## Check the assignment
check_taper_models(model = tree$model, spcd = tree$spcd)
#> [1] row     id      status  problem input  
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

Fitting taper equations creates local models for the same stem functions.
